why: This hour carries 396's name, but nearly all of it was 395's work: round 3 of 395's checks, the four tooling fixes, ticking and posting the answer on #6. That work was already judged at hour:395-shrine-building-costs@1 and @2. On 396 itself the session applied the round-1 spec fixes (06:50), got FAITHFUL at spec-fidelity round 2 (07:06), wrote the plan and sent it for plan review (07:07-07:08). There was no loop, no edit made and unmade, and no packing: this is cost research with no size, spacing or band in play. The one waste was guard churn. `pair: step-back-due` refused 395's round-3 wave twice (about 50 refused dispatches at 06:50 and 06:52-06:53) after hour:395@2 had already been ruled, because `.specify/feature.json` still named 397 from the overnight claim. The session hand-wrote that file twice, to 395 at 06:53 and to 396 at 07:08, and the second write is what opened this step-back. 396's hour clock also ran from its claim while the session worked only on 395, so this window repeats an hour already judged. Once the clock follows the feature being worked, that goes away.
what: Go on as planned: 396's plan review is next, then its search passes and implementation.
tooling_fix: Make `make step-back` and `make arbiter-ruled` (for hour: triggers) refuse, naming the one command that realigns them, when `.specify/feature.json` names a different feature from `SPECIFY_FEATURE`, and add a `make use-feature F=NNN` target to replace hand-writing feature.json, so the `pair: step-back-due` guard checks the clock of the feature the ruling just settled rather than a feature left over from an earlier claim.

note: make use-feature F=NNN writes .specify/feature.json; make step-back refuses, naming make use-feature, while feature.json names a different feature from the exported SPECIFY_FEATURE (checkpoint.misaligned)
